prompt:
Sprite sheet for a 2D side-view narrative game: ten figures of the same character, brushed by hand in black ink. The first reference image gives the exact layout and the exact poses: ten figures in two rows of five, all at the same scale, the feet of each row on the same baseline. Figures one to eight (in reading order) are a walk cycle to the right in strict side view; figure nine stands still in side view, both feet flat on the ground; figure ten has turned three-quarters towards the viewer. Copy every pose, the positions of both legs and feet, the arms, the parcel and the satchel, and the place and size of each figure exactly from the first reference; only the drawing changes. The second reference image only shows the costume, the face and the proportions of the character: do not copy its drawing style, its colours, its outlines or its three-view layout. The third reference image shows the brush marks of the game (bold strokes with dry-brush streaks, pale washes, round ink dots): draw the figures with the same brush and the same ink, but do not copy any of its marks.

Drawing technique: a loose, spontaneous brush sketch by an East Asian ink painter (sumi-e figure painting), not a clean illustration. Every contour is a single loaded stroke of a soft pointed brush: thick, as wide as the eye, where the brush is pressed on the shadow side, tapering to a hairline where it lifts, with dry-brush breaks and flecks of white paper; on the lit side the contour is left out and the shape is defined only by the wash. The dark fur of arms, legs, back and eye stripes is painted with one or two broad wet strokes of the side of the brush, with visible bristle streaks and uneven ink, not filled evenly. The cap and the vest are one quick medium grey wash each, slightly uneven, bleeding a little at the edges; the satchel and the parcel one pale grey wash with one dark accent stroke; the shirt, the white face stripes and the belly are bare white paper. The scarf is one wash of vermilion red, darker where the wash pooled, with a few quick strokes for the fringe. No other colours at all: no green, no brown, no cream. No fur texture, no knitted pattern, no hatching, no smooth shading, no highlights; eyes as small black dots, the nose one black dot. Draw a soft, natural badger body as in the second reference, not the blocky shapes or the pointed tail of the 3D figures in the first reference. The same brush, the same ink tones and the same level of detail in every figure. Not a pen drawing, not a cartoon with thin uniform outlines, not a 3D render, not a watercolour in many colours.

The badger courier: an original mascot character, a stout, short-legged badger with a broad black-and-white striped face, wearing a dark green peaked cap with a brass button, a dark green vest with pockets over a cream shirt with rolled-up sleeves, a long red knitted scarf, a brown leather satchel on a shoulder strap, and a brown paper parcel tied with string under one arm.

The figures are isolated on a fully transparent background: everything outside the figures is transparent; the bare paper inside each figure (shirt, white face, belly) is opaque white. No paper texture or paper colour outside the figures, no ground line, no shadow on the floor, no seal stamps, no text.

No text, letters, numbers, signatures, watermarks or logos anywhere in the image. No real places, brands, franchises or recognisable characters from existing games or films.

Image format: landscape 3:2.
